data: 大学[だいがく]に 近[ちか]くて 便利[べんり]だって 言[い]っても、 家賃[やちん]が 高[たか]すぎるから、 この 部屋[へや]は 借[か]りられない。
Even if its location is close to the university, the rent for this room is too high for me to rent it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-plain {と/って} 言っても "although ~ say/said that ~; even though ~ say/said that ~" Its used to clarify what has just been said in order to avoid misunderstanding. って is used in place of と in casual conversation or writing.
郵便[ゆうびん] 局[きょく]に 行[い]って来[こ]なくちゃん ないから、 ちょっと ここで 待[ま]ってて。
I've gotta run to the post office, so wait here for a sec.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: These patterns express the idea of obligation. Although the two patterns are interchangeable, there is a subtle difference between ならない and いけない. That is, ならない is commonly used when the speaker states his/her sense of obligation while いけない is commonly used when the sense of obligation is directed towards the hearer (i.e. when the speaker wants to impose a certain obligation on the hearer). The following contracted forms are used in casual conversation: なきゃならない -> なきゃなんない なくちゃならない -> なくちゃんなんない --- 英訳 [English translation]: have to; must; should --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜なければ{いけない/ならない} 〜なくては{いけない/ならない}
よく 切[き]れない 包丁[ほうちょう]は かえって 危[あぶ]ないよ。
Dull knives are actually all the more dangerous, you know.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
かえって "on the contrary; rather"
危[あぶ]ないですから、 この フィンスの 中[なか]に 決[けっ]して 入[はい]っては いけませんよ。
It's dangerous, so you absolutely must not enter into this fenced area.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
決して{ANa/ANo/N} {では/じゃ} { ない／なかった／ありません／ありませんでした}
将来[しょうらい]は、 ヨーロッパ、 あるいは、 アジアで 仕事[しごと]が できたらいいと 思[おも]っている。
I think it'd be nice if I can work in Europe or Asia in the future.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1(、N2、〜）あるいは Nn "or; either ~ or ~" あるいは is used to connect alternatives. It is usually used in formal speech or written language.
将来[しょうらい]は、 自分[じぶん]の 能力[のうりょく]を 生[い]かす ことが 出来[でき]る 会社[かいしゃ]で 働[はたら]きたい。
In the future, I want to work at a company that puts my skills to good use.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
生かす "make the most of; make the best use of; use effectively; maintain" 生かす means literally "to keep alive," but it is also used to mean "to make the most of one's ability, etc"
将来[しょうらい]、 日本[にほん]の 会社[かいしゃ]で 働[はたら]きたいと 思[おも]っている。 その ためには もっと 日本[にほん]語[ご]が 上手[じょうず]にならなくては いけない。
In the future, I want to work at a Japanese company. For that purpose, I need to become more skilled at Japanese.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ため(に) is preceded by a noun or the non-past form of a verb, it indicates either purpose or reason/cause. In different contexts, Noun のため(に) also indicates benefit. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in order to; to; for the purpose of; for; for the sake of --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nのため(に) N1のためのN2 Verb plainため(に) Verb plainためのN
将来[しょうらい]、 小[しょう]学校[がっこう]の 先生[せんせい]に なりたいと 思[おも]っています。 そこで、 ボランティアで 子供[こども]達[たち]を 教[おし]えてみる ことに しました。
I'm thinking that I want to become an elementary school teacher in the future, so I've decided to try teaching children on a volunteer basis.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1, そこで, S2. "Because of that; therefore; so" そこで is used to indicate and action (to be) taken because of the situation presented in S1. それで may replace そこで そこで may only replace それで when S2 is a controllable action. ex. 寒かった。それで、見に来た人が少なかった。 only それで can be used here.
A: スミスさんは、 将来[しょうらい] 日本[にほん]の 会社[かいしゃ]で 働[はたら]くのが 夢[ゆめ]なんだって。 B: へー、 スミスさんが そんな 夢[ゆめ]を 持[も]っているなんて、 絶対[ぜったい] 知[し]らなかった。
A: They say Ms. Smith's dream is to work at a Japanese company in the future. B: Really? I had no idea she had a dream like that.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
（そんな／あんな／こんな）N そんな／あんな： Means: that kind of ~; ~like that あんな： Means: this kind of ~; ~ like this these words are synonymous with そういう、ああいう、こういう respectively and are a bit more colloquial than them.
この 大学[だいがく]では、 日本[にほん]語[ご]、 あるいは、 英語[えいご]で 卒業[そつぎょう] 論文[ろんぶん]を 書[か]く ことに なっている。
At this university, senior theses are expected to be written in either Japanese or English.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1(、N2、〜）あるいは Nn "or; either ~ or ~" あるいは is used to connect alternatives. It is usually used in formal speech or written language.
せっかく 4[よん]年間[ねんかん]も 日本[にほん]語[ご]を 勉強[べんきょう] したのに、 大学[だいがく]を 卒業[そつぎょう] してから あまり 使[つか]わなかったら、 だんだん 忘[わす]れてしまった。
I put in four whole years studying Japanese, but I haven't used it much since I graduated from the university, so now bit by bit I'm forgetting it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
だんだん "gradually; little by little; bit by bit" だんだん is used to indicate that a state changes gradually. Thus, it often occurs with ~ていく; 〜てくる；〜くなる；〜になる；〜ようになる
とうとう 博士[はかせ] 論文[ろんぶん]が 完成[かんせい] した。 5[ご]年[ねん]も かかってしまった。
My doctoral dissertation is finally complete. It took me five whole years.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

とうとう V "finally; at (long) last; eventually; in the end; after all" とうとう indicates that an expected situation has occurred after an extended period of time. The adverb ついに is similar to とうとう and can be used in the place of とうとう. ついに is more formal.
一方[いっぽう] 通行[つうこう]の 道[みち]だと いう ことを 知[し]らないで、 逆[ぎゃく]の 方向[ほうこう]に 進[すす]んでしまい、 警察[けいさつ]に つかまってしまった。
I went against traffic, not realizing it was a one-way street, and ended up getting pulled over by the police.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

逆 の N。 "opposite N; the reverse of N" 逆 is used to indicate that X's way of doing something is the opposite of Y's way of doing it, or that the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way Y is or the way Y happens. In different contexts, ぎゃくindicates that X's way of doing something, the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way which is common, expected or intended.
チーズや ヨーグルトは 牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]から 出来[でき]ます。
Cheese and yogurt are made from milk.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: {で/から}できる means "to be made of/from/out of." から indicates that the material(s) from which something is made is not immediately obvious. できる is used in generic statements while できている is used when describing something specific. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~でできる = be made of; be made out of ~からできる = be made from --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N {で / から} {できる / できている} --- The difference between raw material and material/ingredient is whether the material undergoes qualitative transformation in the production process. Typically, when there is a qualitative change, から is used; when there is no qualitative change, で is used.
私[わたし]の 知[し]っている 限[かぎ]り、 外国[がいこく]人[じん]が 使[つか]いやすい 日本[にほん]語[ご]の 辞書[じしょ]は ないんですよ。
As far as I know, there's no Japanese dictionary that's easy for non-native speakers to use.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain 限り "as long as; as far as; while; until; unless; as much as; as much as (one can)" this grammar is used when something is the case or is true as long as the condition in X holds true. It is also used to indicate the extent to which one can do something or one knows something. (as far as one can; as far as one knows)
A: あれっ、 その 足[あし]、 どう したの。 B: 実[じつ]は さあ、 昨日[きのう]、 階段[かいだん]で 転[ころ]んじゃってさあ、 骨[ほね]、 折[お]っちゃったんだよ。
A: Oh, what did you do to your leg? B: Actually, I fell down some stairs yesterday and ended up breaking it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

phrase/clause/sentence さ(あ) "(you know)" さ occurs after phrases, clauses, or sentences in very casual conversation. One function is to catch the hearer's attention, but it is also used as a filler with no meaning.
日曜[にちよう] 日[び]の ピクニックは お天気[てんき] 次第[しだい]ですよ。 雨[あめ]が 降[ふ]れば 来週[らいしゅう]に 延期[えんき] される そうです。
The picnic this Sunday is dependant on the weather. I heard that if it rains, it'll be postboned until next week.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N次第だ "depend on N" When 次第 is affixed to nouns, it means "depend on."
この （）に 入[い]れるのは、 助詞[じょし]でなくては いけません。
What you insert within this ( ) must be a particle.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: These patterns express the idea of obligation. Although the two patterns are interchangeable, there is a subtle difference between ならない and いけない. That is, ならない is commonly used when the speaker states his/her sense of obligation while いけない is commonly used when the sense of obligation is directed towards the hearer (i.e. when the speaker wants to impose a certain obligation on the hearer). The following contracted forms are used in casual conversation: なきゃならない -> なきゃなんない なくちゃならない -> なくちゃんなんない --- 英訳 [English translation]: have to; must; should --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜なければ{いけない/ならない} 〜なくては{いけない/ならない}
暖[あたた]かみ
warmth
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

A-stem み (only some A can use this form) "~ness" When み is affixed to the stems of i-adjectives, a noun is formed. み - affixed nouns usually refer to an aspect of something/someone directly perceived by the speaker and are often more emotivethan さ-affixed nouns.
夏[なつ]に なって、 だんだん 暖[あたた]かくなってきた。
Spring has come, and it's gradually gotten warmer.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
だんだん "gradually; little by little; bit by bit" だんだん is used to indicate that a state changes gradually. Thus, it often occurs with ~ていく; 〜てくる；〜くなる；〜になる；〜ようになる
これから、 もっと 暖[あたた]かくなって行[い]きます。
From now on, it's going to grow warmer.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-teくる and V-teいく indicate the temporal or spatial direction of an action from the speaker's viewpoint. V-teくる is used when an action appears to be directed toward the speaker, and V-teいく is used when it appears to be directed away from the speaker. V-teくる often indicates that an action or process began in the past and is continuing in the present, or that something has begun to take place. V-teいく, on the other hand, often expresses an action or state that will continue from the present into the future. In other uses, 来る and 行くfollowing V-te maintain their original meanings, i.e., "to come" and "to go." --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-teくる = have V-ed; begin to; become; grow V−teいく = go on V-ing; continue; become; grow --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te来る/行く
最近[さいきん]、 ちょっと 暖[あたた]かくなってきました。
It's gotten a little warmer recently.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-teくる and V-teいく indicate the temporal or spatial direction of an action from the speaker's viewpoint. V-teくる is used when an action appears to be directed toward the speaker, and V-teいく is used when it appears to be directed away from the speaker. V-teくる often indicates that an action or process began in the past and is continuing in the present, or that something has begun to take place. V-teいく, on the other hand, often expresses an action or state that will continue from the present into the future. In other uses, 来る and 行くfollowing V-te maintain their original meanings, i.e., "to come" and "to go." --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-teくる = have V-ed; begin to; become; grow V−teいく = go on V-ing; continue; become; grow --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te来る/行く
今[いま]の ままだと、 地球[ちきゅう] 温暖[おんだん]化[か]は 止[と]まらない。
If things keep going like this, global warming won't come to an end.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N のままだ "remain the same as ~" まま indicates that the state of X remains unchanged or that someone does something without changing the current state of X.
地球[ちきゅう] 温暖[おんだん]化[か]の 問題[もんだい]は もっと 大[おお]きくなっていくのでは ないでしょうか。
I think that the problem of global warming may grow bigger from now on.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This ending indicates the speaker's conjecture and is used to express an opinion in an indecisive fashion. Although the negative form ではない is used, there is no negative meaning. のではない{だろう/でしょう}か are used only in written language, and のではないだろうか is the more formal form. ん{ではないでしょうか/じゃないかな} are used only in spoken language. んじゃないかな is more casual. --- 英訳 [English translation]: I think that ~; Isn't it that~? --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Sのではないでしょうか。
へえ。 日本[にほん]では 四国[しこく]に 住[す]んでおられたんですか。 暖[あたた]かいし、 海[うみ]も きれいだし、 いい 所[ところ]ですよね。
Wow, you lived in Shikoku when you were in Japan? It's a nice place, isn't it? The weather's warm and the sea's beautiful, too.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

る-verbs: V-masu + られる Passive forms of verbs are used to indicate politeness when the speaker refers to the actions of the hearer or someone to whom the speaker wants to show deference. However, this use of passive forms does not indicate as high a level of politeness as おV-masu になる or special honorific verbs like いらっしゃる and めし上がる。 Note that the polite form of the auxilliary verb いる is not いられる, but おられる. The auxilliary verb おられる is less polite than いらっしゃる。 sentence final よね indicates the speaker is unsure about the statement.
今年[ことし]は 12[じゅうに]月[がつ]に なっても なかなか 寒[さむ]くならない。 地球[ちきゅう] 温暖[おんだん]化[か]の せいだろうか。
This year it just hasn't gotten cold even though it's already December. I wonder if it's because of global warming.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

なかなか V-nai ない "not easily; not readily; difficult to~; slow to; to refuse to" なかなか with V-nai is usually used when something desirable doesn't happen easily or when something that is supposed to happen doesn't happen.
地球[ちきゅう]の 未来[みらい]を 考[かんが]えた とき、 何[なに]よりも まず 初[はじ]めに 地球[ちきゅう] 温暖[おんだん]化[か]が 問題[もんだい]に されるべきだ。
When thinking about the future of the Earth, global warming is the issue that must be addressed before anything else.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N/NP が問題に {される／なる} "X becomes an issue; X is brought up as an issue; X is questioned; X is called into question." X を 問題にする means "to bring X up as an issue" or "to question X." This phrase is often used in the passive form Xが問題にされる. Xが問題になる is also common. The meaning is the same as that of the passive version.
明日[あした]は 他[た]の 約束[やくそく]が あるから、 行[い]かないって 言[い]ったでしょ。 忘[わす]れたの？
I told you that I've already got plans, so I can't go. Did you forget?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: でしょう and だろう with rising intonation are used to elicit the hearer's confirmation. でしょう is the polite version of だろう. In casual conversation, male speakers use だろう and female speakers use でしょう. In more casual situations, the final う tends to drop. Note: でしょう and だろう with falling intonation indicate conjecture. --- 英訳 [English translation]: tag question(e.g. isn't it?; wasn't it?; aren't they?; is he?; are they?) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~だろう, ~でしょう
両親[りょうしん]が 亡[な]くなった 後[あと]、 私[わたし]は 兄[あに]と ともに 二人[ふたり]で 助[たす]け合[あ]って 生[い]きてきました。
Since my parents died, my older brother and I have helped each other (and managed) to get by.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Nと共に "with; along with; as" indicates that someone does something or that something happens with N.
私[わたし]の 血液[けつえき]型[がた]は Ａです、 母[はは]は ＡＢ型[がた]で 父[ちち]は Ｏ型[がた]、 弟[おとうと]は Ｂ型[がた]です。
My blood type is A, but my mother's is AB, my father's is O, and my little brother's is B.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 型 is a suffix meaning "style, type, model, etc." It is commonly used to describe the shape, type, model, or newness of an object. The preceding elements are mostly nouns, but some adjectival kanji characters can also precede 型(e.g. 大, 新, 薄). --- 英訳 [English translation]: style; type; pattern; make; model; design --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N + 型だ b. N1 + 型(の)N2
父[ちち]は １０[じゅう]年[ねん] 前[まえ]に 亡[な]くなった。 それ 以来[いらい]、 母[はは]は 一人[ひとり]で 私[わたし]達[たち] 兄弟[きょうだい]を 育[そだ]ててくれた。
My father passed away ten years ago. Since then, my mother has reared my brother and me on her own.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
VN/Nいらい "since ~" It is used with V-te or VN referring to an action in the past, or with N indicating a specific time in the past.
ケーキを 作[つく]ろうと したけれど、 卵[たまご]が なかったから、 作[つく]れなかった。
I tried to make a cake, but there weren't any eggs, so I couldn't.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-volとした, the past form of V-volとする(to try to do ~), is used in situations when someone had made an attempt to do something but failed, where someone was going to do something but didn't, or where something happened when someone was going to do something. --- 英訳 [English translation]: V-volとした{が／けれど} = tried to ~, but; was going to ~, but V-volとしたら = when ~ was going to ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-volとした{が／けれど}: 行こうとした{が／けれど／ら}; 食べようとした{が／けれど／ら}
漢字[かんじ]って、 覚[おぼ]えても 直[す]ぐ 忘[わす]れちゃうよね。
As for Kanji, even if you memorize them, you forget them immediately (without even intending to), don't you?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: って is a colloquial topic marker. It often appears in questions. In written language, は can be used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Speaking of ~, As for ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N って
漢字[かんじ]が もっと 簡単[かんたん]に 覚[おぼ]えられたらいいのになあ。
I wish it were easier to memorize kanji.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S-plain.past (V are typically volitional) らいいのになあ。 is used to express the speaker's wish, which, in this structure, is usually counterfactual. なあ serves to make it more emotive. Verbs, usually volitional, refer to the SPEAKER'S actions. This is a very casual expression.
この 漢字[かんじ] 何[なん]回[かい] 覚[おぼ]えても、 すぐに 忘[わす]れてしまう。
No matter how many times I memorize this kanji I forget it right away.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: When ても is used with a question word, the phrase means: "no matter" or "without regard to." --- 英訳 [English translation]: no matter what/who/when/where/how --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ QW(prt)+V-teも
漢字[かんじ]が 難[むずか]しいと 思[おも]っている 学生[がくせい]は 少[すく]なくない。
There are more than a few students who think that kanji are difficult.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N {は／が／も} 少なくない "many; much; plenty of; not a few' 少なくない is a double negative meaning "many; much" and is commonly used in written language. It cannot modify nouns. For ex. 少なくない人 is a BAD expression.
私[わたし]に とって、 読[よ]み物[もの]が 難[むずか]しいか どうかは、 漢字[かんじ]の 多[おお]さに よります。
As it concerns me, whether I find reading material difficult or not depends on the "numerousness" of the kanji.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate that something differs depending on the situation, location, time, etc. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~によって違う = differ depending on ~ / due to ~ による = depend on, due to, according to --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {Noun/Question Word ~ か/ ~かどうか}は Noun に {よって違う / よる }
朝[あさ]から 晩[ばん]まで コンピュータの スクリーンを 見[み]続[つづ]けているので、 目[め]が 悪[わる]くなってしまった。
I'm continuously looking at a computer screen from morning till night, so my eyes have gotten bad.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V−masu 続く Means: continue to; continue V-ing; go on V-ing; keep (on) V-ing;all the way; all the time This phrase is used when the subject continues doing something volitionally.
母[はは]が 病気[びょうき]だったので、 （母[はは]の） 代[か]わりに 私[わたし]が 晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]を 作[つく]りました。
Because mom was ill, I made dinner instead.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: の代わりに is used to present something/someone that is replacing or has replaced something/someone. When the context is clear, Noun の can be omitted. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in place of; instead of; to make up for --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nの代わりに
日本[にほん]語[ご]の 宿題[しゅくだい]は 今晩[こんばん] しますが、 後[あと]に 宿題[しゅくだい]は 明日[あした] する つもりです。
I'm going to do my Japanese homework tonight, but I'll do the rest of my homework tomorrow.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

後のN "the remaining ~; the remainder of ~; the rest of ~" This use of 後 should be distinguished from 後 in the following example, where 後 means "~more." In this use, の cannot occur after 後. このプロジェクトには後三人必要だ。
北海道[ほっかいどう]の ホスト ファミリーの お母[かあ]さんは 元気[げんき]かなあ。 今晩[こんばん]、 電話[でんわ] してみよう。
I wonder how my host mom in Hokkaido is. I'll give her a call tonight.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 〜かなあ is a sentence final particle which indicates that the sentence is a self-addressed question or a question addressed to the speaker's in-group member(s). It is used only in casual language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: I wonder ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜かな(あ)
毎晩[まいばん] コーラス 部[ぶ]の 練習[れんしゅう]が 有[あ]るので、 勉強[べんきょう]を し始[はじ]めるのは いつも １０[じゅう]時[じ]過[す]ぎだ。

スミスさんは 日本[にほん]に １０[じゅう]年[ねん]も 住[す]んでいたから、 日本[にほん]語[ご]が 上手[じょうず]に 話[はな]せるに 違[ちが]い ない。

説明 [explanation]: This structure indicates that the speaker is certain that something is true or is the case. It is used primarily in written language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: must; I'm sure/certain that ~; It is certain that ~; I'm certain that ~; be sure to V. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜に違いない

S(という)ことになる Means: end up (with); mean that ~; cause This grammar is usually preceded by 1 of 3 types of sentences, here is is (1) a topic phrase, and indicates that the (non-) action, even or situation stated in the preceding phrase/clause leads to a logical conclusion or a certain situation.
もし 文法[ぶんぽう]が 間違[まちが]ってたら、 直[なお]してくれる？

作文[さくぶん]を 書[か]いた ことは 書[か]いたけれど、 まだ 間違[まちが]いが たくさん あるから 書[か]き直[なお]さなくては いけない。

こんなに たくさんの 人[ひと]が 読[よ]んでいるのだから、 面白[おもしろ]い 本[ほん]であるに 違[ちが]い ない。

〜である/~ではない is the formal plain form of だ and can be affixed to nouns and -な／-の adjectives. である is used in formal writing. In very formal speech the polite form であります／ではありません may be used. である can occur before nouns in relative clauses while だ cannot.
試験[しけん]が 終[お]わってから、 答[こた]えを 間違[まちが]えた ことに 気[き]が つきました。

S ことに気がつく means: notice (that~); realize that ~ Notice that the presence of こと in a sentence using this grammar may not always be the nominalizer meaning "that." It could be a noun meaning "thing" following the noun-typed usage of this grammar.
Wikipediaは 何[なに]かを 調[しら]べる ときに とても 便利[べんり]だ。だが、 間違[まちが]った 情報[じょうほう]も たくさん あるので、 注意[ちゅうい] した 方[ほう]が いい。

{ANa/N/QW} (なん）だっけ っけ is a question marker used in very casual conversation. Note that after the non-past forms of V, A and ~ない, んだ must be used before っけ。

{ANA/N} じゃなかった（んだ）っけ っけ is a question marker used in very casual conversation. Note that after the non-past forms of V, A and ~ない, んだ must be used before っけ。
デートを し始[はじ]めて、 彼[かれ]の ことが ますます 好[す]きになった。

ますます Adv "more and more; -er and -er; increasingly; even more; even -er; still more; still -er" ますます occurs with verbs, the adverbial forms of adjectives and adverbs. It indicates that something happens to an even greater (or lesser) degree than before. ますます is NOT used for future controllable events. For example, it cannot replace もっともっと in もっともっとがんばって下さい。
彼[かれ]は、 デートの たびに おいしい レストランに 連[つ]れて行[い]ってくれる。

Nのたびに "every time; each time; on every ~; whenever" たびに expresses the idea that each time someone does something, something else takes place. When たびに is modified by a noun, the noun refers to an action or certain time.
彼[かれ]と 私[わたし]の 考[かんが]えは まったく 同[おな]じだ。
His idea and mine are exactly the same.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

まったく {V/A/ANo/(の)N/Ano} "totally; utterly; entirely; completely; extremely; absolutely; really" used for emphasis in affirmative sentences. often used to express the speaker's emotion. In negative sentences, it indicates complete negation. It is used with verbs (often in potential form) and i-adjectives in negative sentences. まったく〜（という）わけではない indicates partial negation.
彼[かれ]と 別[わか]れても がっかり する こと ないよ。 もっと いい 人[ひと]が すぐ 見[み]つかるから。

Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-plain.non-past すること（は）ない "don't have to ~; don't need to ~; It's not necessary to ~; There is no need to ~" In casual conversation the は may drop.
なぜ 彼[かれ]は 私[わたし]の ことを 愛[あい]してくれないのだろうか。 私[わたし]は 彼[かれ]が こんなに 好[す]きなのに。
Why doesn't he love me back when I love him so much?

Sの（だろう／でしょう）か Means: I wonder ~ Indicates a self-addressed question which can either be a yes-no question or a wh- question.

Grammar,扉,Intermediate
決して{ANa/ANo/N} {では/じゃ} { ない／なかった／ありません／ありませんでした}

ずっと "all the time; all along; all the way; all through ~; throughout~; ever (since); never (since)" ずっと means that a state or action is ongoing, from one point in time to another point in time (often the moment of speech)

10/20/30/etc. ＋ 代 "one's teens/twenties/ thirties/etc." The suffix 代 is used with ten or its multiples to describe someone's approximate age.

Personal pronoun ら "these; those; they; -s; and others" [plural dem. pronouns can be used in polite speech] The plural marker ら is often used with demonstrative pronouns and certain personal pronouns. plural personal pronouns are not used in polite speech.

説明 [explanation]: (1) This construction is used to state either a purpose or the way in which something is to be done. In XようにY, X represents a state or event which is beyond the control of the subject of Y. The verb form before ように is often a potential form or a negative form. (2) In the similar construction XためにY, X represents an action which can be controlled by the subject of Y, while XようにY implies that a certain consequence (X) will arise as the result of an action (Y). --- 英訳 [English translation]: so that ~; in such a way that~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.nonpastように

Nからすると "judging from~" Introduces the source or basis for the speaker's conjecture or judgment. The information can be of any sort including visual or verbal.

It indicates either that the speaker (or the subject of the sentence) did not actively make the decision or that he/she is viewing the decision from the standpoint of an outsider. 説明 [explanation]: These patterns express the idea of obligation. Although the two patterns are interchangeable, there is a subtle difference between ならない and いけない. That is, ならない is commonly used when the speaker states his/her sense of obligation while いけない is commonly used when the sense of obligation is directed towards the hearer (i.e. when the speaker wants to impose a certain obligation on the hearer). S + という点で "in that ~" 点 is used to mean "point" (in the sense of a single, fact, idea or opinion in an argument, discussion, etc.), "aspect," or "viewpoint/standpoint."

In casual conversation, male speakers use だろう and female speakers use でしょう. In more casual situations, the final う tends to drop. V-plain.non-past ほど "to the extent that~ ; so~ that ~ (almost)~; not as ~ as N; to (this/that) degree; (this/that) much" The particle ほど is used to express the degree of a state. When a sentence precedes ほど, the element just before ほど is a verb.
疲[つか]れていたので、 テレビを つけっぱなしにして 寝[ね]てしまった。
I was tired, so I fell asleep without turning off the TV.

V-masuっぱなしにする "keep V-ing; leave" This is used when someone or something keeps doing X or someone did X but did not finish the action properly. As in this case, Vっぱなし is often used to describe an undesirable situation, but this is not always the case. Not used in formal language.
疲[つか]れていたので、 電気[でんき]を つけた まま 寝[ね]てしまった。 ネクタイも した ままだった。
I was tired, so I fell asleep with the lights still on. I left my tie on, too.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Aまま（で）V "V with ~; V while ~; V as (it is); V without ~" まま indicates that the state of X remains unchanged or that someone does something without changing the current state of X.
私[わたし]たちは 話[はなし]も 出来[でき]ないほど 疲[つか]れていた。
We were so tired we couldn't even speak.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-plain.non-past ほど "to the extent that~ ; so~ that ~ (almost)~; not as ~ as N; to (this/that) degree; (this/that) much" The particle ほど is used to express the degree of a state. When a sentence precedes ほど, the element just before ほど is a verb.
昨日[きのう]は 疲[つか]れていたから、 1[いち]日[にち]中[ちゅう] ほとんど 寝[ね]ていました。
I was tired yesterday, so I slept almost all day long.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
ほとんど V Means "almost all; most of (it, the time, etc.)" It is only used with the amount of something is the issue.
あの 仕事[しごと]は、 立[た]ちっぱなしの 仕事[しごと]だから、 疲[つか]れるに 違[ちが]い ない。
You don't get to sit down at that job, so it'll definitely tire you out.

V-masu っぱなしの N "keep V-ing; leave" This is used when someone or something keeps doing X or someone did X but did not finish the action properly. As in this case, Vっぱなし is often used to describe an undesirable situation, but this is not always the case. Not used in formal language.
私[わたし]に とって 一番[いちばん] 大切[たいせつ]な ものは 私[わたし]の 猫[ねこ]だが、 猫[ねこ]に とって 一番[いちばん] 大切[たいせつ]な ものは 食[た]べ物[もの]の ようだ。
My cat is the most important thing in the world to me, but for my cat it seems like the most important thing in the world is food.

説明 [explanation]: Xにとって means "to X; for X" in a context where something (or someone) is important to X, or is necessary, useful, good, difficult, etc. for X. X is often a person, a geographic unit or an organization. --- 英訳 [English translation]: for, to, from the standpoint of, as far as ... is concerned --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nに取って
あの 人[ひと]は 動物[どうぶつ]の 言葉[ことば]が 分[わ]かるんです。 猫[ねこ]や 犬[いぬ]とさえ 会話[かいわ]が できるんですよ。
That person can understand what animals say. He can even communicate with cats and dogs.

N (prt) さえ Means: even さえ is an emphatic particle. In non-conditional clauses it means "even." When さえ is used, the particle が never occurs, を usually does not occur, へ and the directional に are optional, and the other particles, including the LOCATIONAL に, で、と and から are mandatory.
人[ひと]は 失敗[しっぱい] して 初[はじ]めて、 自分[じぶん]の した ことが 間違[まちが]えていた ことに 気[き]が つく。
It's when people fail that they first realize that what they'd done was wrong.

N に気がつく。 Means: notice (that~); realize that ~ Notice that the presence of こと in a sentence using this grammar will not always be the nominalizer meaning "thing." It could be the Sこと form for statements using this grammar.
友達[ともだち]が 迎[むか]えに 来[き]たら、 私[わたし]は 帰[かえ]ります。
If/when my friend comes to pick me up, I will leave.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

S1たらS２。 When たら is used, as opposed to (の)なら, S1 must be completed before S2. 説明 [explanation]: なら is used when the speaker supposes that something is the case or is true and makes a statement, suggestion, etc. based on that supposition. の occurs before なら when the supposition is based on what the speaker has heard from someone or learned from the situation. Nなら means "if it is N; N would/could ~." In "S1 なら S2", the action/event in S1 does not have to take place before that in S2. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Nなら = would; could~ S(の)なら = if (it's the case that) ~; if (it's true that) ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~(の)なら
健康[けんこう]の ためには、 朝御飯[あさごはん]は ちゃんと 食[た]べて、 夜[よる]も 6[ろく]時間[じかん] 以上[いじょう] はねた 方[ほう]が いいですよ。
For your health, you'd better eat a proper breakfast every morning and sleep at least six hours every night.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ちゃんと；きちんと "neatly; tidily; properly; adequately; in good order; regularly; without fail" ちゃんと and きちんと both indicate that someone does something neatly, properly, regularly, or without fail (i.e. in the way it is supposed to be done). ちゃんと is more colloquial than きちんと。
フィンランド語[ご]とか トルコ語[ご]とか、 皆[みな]が 余[あま]り 勉強[べんきょう] してない 言葉[ことば]を 勉強[べんきょう] してみたい。
I want to try studying a language not many people learn, like Finnish or Turkish.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: とか is used to list examples non-exhaustively. It is similar to や in meaning when the examples listed are nouns. Unlike や, however, とか can be preceeded by verb phrases. When two or more items are listed, とか after the final item is optional when it is followed by a particle and mandatory otherwise (like in this example). (Note that や does not occur after the final item). In Subject とか Subject とかする, the final とか is not optional. --- 英訳 [English translation]: things/places/etc. like ~; and; or --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Noun とか Noun (とか) b. Sentence-plain とか Sentence-plain とか {する/できる}
お湯[ゆ]を わかしっぱなしで 忘[わす]れて 寝[ね]てしまい、 家事[かじ]に なり そうになった。
I almost started a fire when I forgot about the kettle I had put on and fell asleep.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V-masu っぱなしだ／で "keep V-ing; leave" This is used when someone or something keeps doing X or someone did X but did not finish the action properly. As in this case, Vっぱなし is often used to describe an undesirable situation, but this is not always the case. Not used in formal language.
バスが なかなか 来[こ]ない。 授業[じゅぎょう]に 遅[おく]れてしまい そうだ。 困[こま]ったなあ。
The bus just won't come. It looks like I'll be late for class. What should I do?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

なかなか V-nai ない "not easily; not readily; difficult to~; slow to; to refuse to" なかなか with V-nai is usually used when something desirable doesn't happen easily or when something that is supposed to happen doesn't happen.
ルームメートは、 毎日[まいにち] 寝[ね]てばっかり いる。 授業[じゅぎょう]に 行[い]かなくても いいのかなあ。
My roommate does nothing but sleep everyday. I wonder if he doesn't have to go to his lessons.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V−te ばかりいる。 Means: Nothing But; always; all the time ばかり is used to express the idea that someone does one thing all the time and does nothing else, or that someone chooses just one thing among others when doing something. Ex: 田中さんはマンガばかり読んでいる。 can mean: (= All tanaka does is read comics); (= Tanaka reads only comics); (=When Masao reads, he reads nothing but comics) NOTE: ばっかり is more colloquial than ばかり
授業[じゅぎょう]を 休[やす]む ときは 先生[せんせい]に 連絡[れんらく] しなくては いけない ことに なっているが、 忘[わす]れてしまった。
We're supposed to let the teacher know if we're going to miss a class, but I forgot.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.non-past ことになっている means that something has been decided and the result of the decision is still in effect. It is often used to introduce rules or customs, as well as one's schedule. --- 英訳 [English translation]: be supposed to ~; It is a rule that ~; It's been decided that ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-past ことになっている: {行く/行かない}ことになっている
もし 時間[じかん]が あったら、 明日[あした] 空港[くうこう]に 迎[むか]えに 来[き]てもらえない？
If you have time, could you come and get me at the airport tomorrow?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-te くれる, etc. with rising intonation is used to make request in casual conversation. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Will you ~?; Can you ~?; Could you~? --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-te {くれる / くれない / もらえる / もらえない}
さて、 もう 遅[おそ]いですだら、 今日[きょう]は これで 失礼[しつれい] します。
Well, its already late, so I'm going to excuse myself for today.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

(S1.) さて、S2. "well; now; well now" さて always occurs at the beginning of a sentence and signals that (a) the speaker/writer is beginning a new topic (the new topic and the previous topic may be part of the same discourse) (b) the speaker/writer is going to ask a question about the information just provided, or (c) the speaker is leaving. AS SEEN HERE さてis not used in casual situations.
ダイエットを しているから、 甘[あま]い 物[もの]は なるべく 食[た]べない ようにしています。
I'm on diet, so I'm trying to eat as few sweets as I can.

説明 [explanation]: なるべく with or without an adverb modifies the following verb phrase and adds the meaning "as (much) as possible." When there is no specific adverb after なるべく, it is usually interpreted as "as much as~" or "as often as~." --- 英訳 [English translation]: as much/often as possible; as ~ as possible --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ なるべく
私[わたし]と 両親[りょうしん]の 教[おし]えは いつも 逆[ぎゃく]だ。 どう して こんなに 意見[いけん]が 違[ちが]うのだろう。

X は 逆 だ。 "be opposite; the other way" 逆 is used to indicate that X's way of doing something is the opposite of Y's way of doing it, or that the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way Y is or the way Y happens. In different contexts, ぎゃくindicates that X's way of doing something, the way X is or the way X happens is the opposite of the way which is common, expected or intended.

Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-te しようがない "cannot help V-ing; cannot stop feeling ~; so ~; unbearably ~" てしかたない、てしようがない,etc. literally mean that a situation is such or is occurring and there is no way to escape it. The phrases are used to indicate that the speaker is unable to control his psychological/physiological reactions or bear a sensation or an external situation. しかたがない and しようがない are interchangeable. This use is different from the following example, where the しかたがない means "it cannot be helped; there's nothing one can do." お金がないのだから、留学できないのはしかたがない。
彼[かれ]は 小学[しょうがく]生[せい]だけれど、 かなり 背[せ]が 高[たか]いなあ。 中学[ちゅうがく]生[せい]だと 思[おも]ったよ。
He's an elementary school boy, but he's pretty tall. I thought he was a middle schooler.

かなり "considerably; rather; quite; fairly; pretty; quite a lot; Indicates that the degree of something is not extremely high, but is higher than average.
急[いそ]いでいたので タクシーに 乗[の]ったら、 道[みち]が 混[こ]んでいて、 かえって 遅[おそ]くなってしまった。
I took a taxi because I was in a hurry, but the roads were crowded and I ended up even later (than I would've been otherwise).

かえって "on the contrary; rather"
腹[はら]の 立[た]つ ことには、 私[わたし]、 彼[かれ]が 好[す]きです。
What makes me angry is that I like him.

V.plain ことに “It is~ that~; I am/We are ~ that ~; To my ~" ことに is used to express the speaker's feeling or subjective judgment about what is said in the main clause. ことに can only be used with a limited set of words.
小[ちい]さい 猫[ねこ]の 声[こえ]は、 赤[あか]ちゃんが 泣[な]いている ように 聞[き]こえます。
The voice of a small cat sounds like a crying baby.

説明 [explanation]: ように is used when (1) X resembles Y, (2) when X is as Y shows, says, explains, etc. or (3) when X does something as shown/said/explained, etc. in/by Y. --- 英訳 [English translation]: like; as; as if --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N のように V-plain ように
赤[あか]ちゃんが 朝[あさ]まで 泣[な]き続[つづ]けたので、 お母[かあ]さんは 全然[ぜんぜん] 寝[ね]られなかった。
The baby kept crying until morning, so its mother got no sleep.

V−masu 続く Means: continue to; continue V-ing; go on V-ing; keep (on) V-ing;all the way; all the time This phrase is used when the subject continues doing something volitionally.
原爆[げんばく]の 恐[おそ]ろしさは いまだに 忘[わす]れる ことが できない。
I still can't forget the horrors of the atomic bomb.

未だに "still; (not ~) yet" indicates that someone of something is in the same state as he/she/it was some time ago. This form is primarily used in written language. In spoken language まだ is used.
広島[ひろしま]県[けん]には 戦争[せんそう]の 恐[おそ]ろしさと 平和[へいわ]の 大切[たいせつ]さを 伝[つた]える 原爆[げんばく] ドームが 有[あ]ります。
Hiroshima Prefecture has the Atomic Bomb Dome, which conveys the horror of war and the importance of peace.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The suffix さ is attached to the stem of an i-adjective or a na-adjective to form a noun. The typical effect is the addition of this suffix "-ness," as in "niceness" or "-ty," as in "rarity." --- 英訳 [English translation]: -ness; -ty --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {A-stem / ANa} + さ: ひろい + さ = ひろさ; さむい + さ = さむさ; 元気さ; 便利さ; (Exception: いい = よさ)
あの 小娘[こむすめ]は、 まるで 子猫[こねこ]の ようだ。
That young girl is just like a kitten.

Sentence ending form: 〜ようだ。 "as if ~ (were/-ed); just like" This structure is used to introduce a simile, i.e., to describe a thing, person, action, etc. by comparing it with a similar thing, person, action, etc. まるで is an emphatic marker.
この お菓子[かし]は、 冷[つめ]たい まま 食[た]べるより、 電子[でんし] レンジで 温[あたた]めた 方[ほう]が おいしく 食[た]べられますよ。
This sweet is better when you warm it up in the microwave instead of just eating it as it is.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Aまま（で）V "V with ~; V while ~; V as (it is); V without ~" まま indicates that the state of X remains unchanged or that someone does something without changing the current state of X.
子供[こども]には、 子供[こども]の 年齢[ねんれい]に 合[あ]った 本[ほん]を 与[あた]えた 方[ほう]が いいですよ。

N1 に会った N2 "N2 suitable for N1"

In the United States, the rules concerning the legal drinking age are different in each state.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
各 + N "each ~; various" A prefix which adds the meaning "each; various." When the referent of the noun after 各 is unknown, it means "various."
私[わたし]が 彼[かれ]の ことが 好[す]きだと いうのは 事実[じじつ]だが、 将来[しょうらい] 彼[かれ]と 結婚[けっこん] しようと 思[おも]っている わけでは ない。
It's true that I like him, but it's not that I'm thinking about marrying him in the future.

S (という）のは事実だ。 "It is {true/a fact that} ~" Used when the speaker wants to claim that something is true or is a fact, or when he/she admits that something is true or a fact. The presence or absence of という does not change the meaning.
あの 二人[ふたり]は とても 仲[なか]が 良[よ]かったから、 卒業[そつぎょう] した 後[あと]、 結婚[けっこん] したに 違[ちが]い ない。
Those two were always so close; I'm sure they got married after graduation.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure indicates that the speaker is certain that something is true or is the case. It is used primarily in written language. --- 英訳 [English translation]: must; I'm sure/certain that ~; It is certain that ~; I'm certain that ~; be sure to V. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜に違いない
火事[かじ]や 地震[じしん]の 場合[ばあい]には、 エレベーターを 使[つか]わないでください。

説明 [explanation]: 場合 is a noun meaning "case, occasion, situation," but with a modifier it forms an adverbial phrase/clause meaning "when; if; in case." 時 can be used in place of 場合 as seen in this example: 分からない {時／場合} は、言って下さい。 However, 場合 cannot replace 時 when 時 refers to a specific time and does not mean "case; occasion; situation," as shown in the example below: 私が行った {時／ｘ場合}には、ミーティングが始まっていた。 --- 英訳 [English translation]: if; when; in case --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ DemA + 場合: {この/その/あの} 場合
日本[にほん]に 住[す]んでいた 時[とき]は 地震[じしん]が 少[すく]なくなかったから、 本[ほん]高[こう]の そばに はねない ようにしていた。
There were more than a few earthquakes when I was living in Japan, so I made sure not to sleep near the bookshelf.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N {は／が／も} 少なくない "many; much; plenty of; not a few' 少なくない is a double negative meaning "many; much" and is commonly used in written language. It cannot modify nouns. For ex. 少なくない人 is a BAD expression.
雪[ゆき]さえ 降[ふ]らなければ、 車[くるま]の 運転[うんてん]は 怖[こわ]くない。
As long as it doesn't snow, driving a car isn't scary.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Noun さえ with a verb conditional form is used when the condition presented in the clause is the only condition to make the statement in the main clause true. さえ replaces が and を in this structure; however, when other particles occur with さえ here, they do not drop. --- 英訳 [English translation]: If~ only ~; If~ just ~; as long as; --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N( = clause X) さえ V-cond (= clause Y)
橋[はし]の 上[うえ]から 真下[ました]に ある 川[かわ]を 見[み]ると、 とても 怖[こわ]い。
From the bridge, if you look straight down at the river, it's really scary.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

真っX where X = adjective or Noun Means: very; pure; totally; right; mid- 真っAdj indicates the degree of something is very high or is at the highest level. 真っNoun indicates the center of a space or time span. The english translation of 真っ varies according to the word that follows it.

This curry is so hot that I can't eat even a bite.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

まったく〜ない "not ~ at all; not ~ in the least" used for emphasis in affirmative sentences. often used to express the speaker's emotion. In negative sentences, it indicates complete negation. It is used with verbs (often in potential form) and i-adjectives in negative sentences. まったく〜（という）わけではない indicates partial negation.
この カレーは かなり 辛[つら]いけれど、 食[た]べられない ことは ない。
This curry is pretty spicy, but not to the extent that I can't eat it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
かなり "considerably; rather; quite; fairly; pretty; quite a lot; Indicates that the degree of something is not extremely high, but is higher than average.
私[わたし]の 家族[かぞく]は、 父[ちち]を はじめ みんな 辛[つら]い 物[もの]が 大好[だいす]きだ。
In my family, everyone loves spicy food, including my dad.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Noun をはじめ is used to present a primary example when mentioning a group of things or people. --- 英訳 [English translation]: beginning with~; starting with ~; including ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nをはじめ
大学[だいがく]院[いん]で 勉強[べんきょう] できるのは、 授業[じゅぎょう]料[りょう]を 払[はら]ってくれる 兄[あに]の おかげだ。
It is due to my elder brother, who pays my tuition, that I'm able to go to graduate school.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N {の/じゃない／だった／じゃなかった} おかげ "because; due to" Both おかげ and せい are dependent nouns indicating cause. The former is used when the cause brings about a desirable result, and the latter when the cause brings about an unwanted result. Both おかげ and せい are dependent nouns indicating cause. The former is used when the cause brings about a desirable result, and the latter when the cause brings about an unwanted result.
忙[いそが]し過[す]ぎて、 寝[ね]る 時間[じかん]さえ ありません。
I'm so busy I don't even have time to sleep.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N (prt) さえ Means: even さえ is an emphatic particle. In non-conditional clauses it means "even." When さえ is used, the particle が never occurs, を usually does not occur, へ and the directional に are optional, and the other particles, including the LOCATIONAL に, で、と and から are mandatory.
せっかくですが、 今日[きょう]は 仕事[しごと]が 忙[いそが]しくて。
This is a rare (event, invitation, etc), but I'm busy with work today...
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

せっかく{ですが／ですけど／だけど／etc} "with effort; at great pain; take the trouble to do ~; ~, which is a rare occasion/event/etc." せっかく is used in 2 situations: (2) when a given opportunity is rare and therefore he/she wants to make use of it; or, in spite of their opportunity, he/she cannot make use of it
どんなに 忙[いそが]しくても、 少[すく]なくとも 6[ろく]時間[じかん] はねた 方[ほう]が いいですよ。
No matter how busy you are, you should get at least 6 hours of sleep.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
少なくとも Number (+Counter) 少なくとも means "at least." It can be used with a noun or number (optionally followed by a counter). When は follows a number (+counter), it emphasizes the number.
先月[せんげつ]は 忙[いそが]しくて、 たった 二日[ふつか]しか、 休[やす]めなかった。
Last month was busy; I could take only two days off.

説明 [explanation]: When the particle は follows a quantifier (i.e., a word such as 3本 or 少し), it adds the meaning "at least." だけは and ぐらいは (or くらいは) after a noun have the same meaning. --- 英訳 [English translation]: at least. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Number (+ Counter) は b. N だけは c. N {ぐらい/くらい}は

S-plain という理由で "because" (lit. for the reason that~) is used to present the reason for a state, event, or action stated in the main clause. The phrase is usually used in written language.

説明 [explanation]: When ため(に) is preceded by an i-adjective or a na-adjective or the past form of a verb, it indicates reason or cause. When it is preceded by the non-past form of a verb or a noun, it means either reason/cause or purpose. The meaning is determined from the context. Whenため(に) means reason/cause, it can be replaced by 〜から or 〜ので, which are less formal than 〜ために. --- 英訳 [English translation]: because; due to --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {この/その/あの}ため(に)

エコカーは 空気[くうき]を 汚[よご]さず、 ガソリン代[だい]も あまり かからない ことから、 環境[かんきょう]に やさしい 車[くるま]だと 言[い]える。
Because eco card don't pollute the air and they keep people from spending a lot of money on gas, you could say that they are environment-friendly.

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.non-pastようにする: indicates one's conscious effort to do something for some purpose. Note that this phrase differs from Vことにする, which indicates one's decision to do something and the action can be either a single or habitual one. --- 英訳 [English translation]: make an effort to~; make an effort so that~; try (one's best) to do ~; try one's best so that~. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-pastようにする: {食べる/食べない}ようにする

ちゃんと；きちんと "neatly; tidily; properly; adequately; in good order; regularly; without fail" ちゃんと and きちんと both indicate that someone does something neatly, properly, regularly, or without fail (i.e. in the way it is supposed to be done). ちゃんと is more colloquial than きちんと。

〜くせに Means: Although~; in spite of the fact that~; and yet~ This conjunction is used when something commonly expected from information in the subordinate clause (i.e. the くせに phrase/clause) does not happen or is not the case. In most situations, くせに expresses the speaker's anger, frustration or disagreement. This emotion is not directed toward the speaker, but toward the hearer or 3rd person. When くせに is used, the subject of the main clause and that of the subordinate clause must be the same. If the subjects differ, you must use なのに、.
キッチンから 流[なが]れてくる においから すると、 今日[きょう]の 晩御飯[ばんごはん]は カレー ライスかなあ。

Nからすると "judging from~" Introduces the source or basis for the speaker's conjecture or judgment. The information can be of any sort including visual or verbal.
